1. Introduction & Background Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) invites sealed proposals for the supply, installation and commissioning of a Produced Water Treatment (PWT) Package at the Bu Hasnah Field Central Processing Facility CPF-2. Produced water arisings at Bu Hasnah are forecast to increase from approximately 21,000 m3/d (2026) to in excess of 29,000 m3/d by 2029 as the field matures under the current water-flood scheme. The existing skim-tank train is hydraulically limited and cannot achieve the disposal-water quality required for re-injection into the Wasia disposal horizon. The new PWT Package shall treat the full forecast produced-water stream to re-injection quality and shall be integrated with the existing CPF-2 utility and control systems. The successful bidder (the "Contractor") shall perform design verification, supply, delivery to site, installation, pre-commissioning, commissioning and performance testing on a lump-sum turnkey basis. Scope summary. One (1) complete PWT package rated 30,000 m3/d net continuous throughput, achieving outlet oil-in-water (OiW) ≤ 10 mg/L (monthly average) and suspended solids ≤ 15 mg/ L, including all inter-unit piping, instrumentation, motor control centre, chemical injection, 2-year operational spares, and integration with the existing DCS (Yokogawa Centum VP). 2. 16 July 2026, 14:00 (UAE time) Tendering portal) Techno-commercial evaluation July – August 2026 Anticipated Letter of Award (LOA) Q4 2026 Not later than 76 weeks after LOA (target 64 Mechanical completion (contractual) weeks) 3. Instructions to Bidders (ITB) 1. Submission. Bids shall be submitted electronically via the ADNOC e-Tendering portal no later than the deadline in Section 2. Late bids will not be opened. Bids shall comprise a single technical volume and a single commercial volume in PDF format. 2. Language & currency. Bids shall be in English. All prices shall be quoted in UAE Dirhams (AED), fixed and firm, inclusive of all duties and fees but exclusive of UAE VAT. Prices quoted in any other currency constitute a commercial deviation; where ADNOC elects to evaluate such a bid, conversion will be made at the UAE Central Bank reference rate of AED 3.6725 / USD. 3. Validity. Bids shall remain valid for 120 calendar days from the submission deadline. 4. Bid bond. An unconditional bank guarantee for 2% of the total bid value, issued or counter- guaranteed by a UAE-licensed bank, valid 150 days, shall accompany the bid. 5. Completeness. Bids omitting any mandatory submission requirement listed in Section 4 shall be deemed conditionally non-compliant and shall be excluded from award consideration; they may be scored for benchmarking purposes only. 6. Arithmetic. In the event of any discrepancy between unit rates, line-item amounts and totals, the corrected sum of line items shall govern and shall be used as the evaluated price. 7. Clarifications. Questions shall be submitted in writing via the portal before the clarification deadline. Responses will be issued to all bidders by numbered bulletin. 8. No contact. Bidders shall not contact ADNOC asset teams directly during the tender period. Canvassing in any form shall result in disqualification. 9. Partial bids / alternates. Partial bids are not accepted. One (1) technical alternate may be offered in addition to a fully compliant base bid. 10. Costs. Bidders bear all costs of bid preparation. ADNOC is not bound to accept the lowest or any bid. Any item marked "Not submitted" renders the bid conditionally non-compliant per ITB clause 5. Code Mandatory document Format D1 Company profile incl. valid UAE/home-country trade licence PDF, max 20 pages D2 Technical proposal with equipment list and datasheets PDF D3 Itemized commercial proposal, priced in AED PDF, itemized table D4 Delivery schedule (Level 2) to mechanical completion PDF or native plan PDF, tabulated by D5 HSE statistics: 3-year TRIR, LTI and fatality record year PDF copy of D6 Valid ICV certificate (MoIAT-certified body) certificate PDF, audited & D7 Audited financial statements (last 2 financial years) signed D8 Bid bond / bank guarantee, 2% of bid value, 150-day validity Original + PDF copy D9 Warranty statement (minimum 24 months from acceptance) PDF, signed Note on ICV. The In-Country Value certificate (D6) must be issued by a MoIAT-certified body and be valid on the bid submission date. The certified ICV score is used directly in the evaluation formula in Section 6.4 — bids without a valid certificate score zero for ICV and fail mandatory screening. 5. Scope of Work & Key Technical Requirements

5.1 Design basis Parameter Requirement Net treatment capacity ≥ 30,000 m3/d (≈ 188,700 bbl/d) at 100% availability, single train or parallel (continuous) trains Inlet oil-in-water (design) up to 650 mg/L (spikes to 1,500 mg/L, 2-hr excursions) Outlet oil-in-water (guarantee ≤ 10 mg/L monthly average, ≤ 15 mg/L daily point) Outlet total suspended solids ≤ 15 mg/L; particle size ≤ 5 μm (98th percentile) Operating temperature /

55 – 78 °C / 3.5 barg design at battery limit pressure H2S in produced water up to 45 ppmw — materials & venting to be sour-service rated (NACE MR0175) Turndown 30% of design flow without performance degradation Availability ≥ 97% with n+1 philosophy on rotating equipment Tie-ins per Exhibit C; DCS integration to Yokogawa Centum VP; F&G to existing Utility & control integration addressable system Warranty Minimum 24 months from provisional acceptance Synthetic dataset - hackathon use only Page 4 of 8

5.2 Battery limits & exclusions Feed from existing degassing boiler drum outlet header (36" CS); treated water to disposal-water booster pump suction header. Power at 11 kV from existing substation SS-04 (Contractor supplies transformers and MCC). Civil piling, permanent camp and disposal wells are excluded. Full details in Exhibits B–E of the tender package. Synthetic dataset - hackathon use only Page 5 of 8

6. Evaluation Criteria & Scoring Methodology Bids passing mandatory screening (Section 4) and meeting the minimum technical requirements (Section 5.1) are scored out of 100 points: Technical 40, Commercial 30, HSE 15, ICV 15. Sub-criteria scored on 0–5 bands convert to points as: points = (band / 5) × weight. All bands are defined numerically below and are applied without discretion. The highest total score is recommended for award.

6.4 In-Country Value — 15 points ICV score = 15 × min( certified ICV %, 60 ) ÷ 60, rounded to 2 decimal places Example: a certified ICV score of 45% earns 15 × 45/60 = 11.25 points. Bids without a valid ICV certificate score 0 and additionally fail mandatory screening (Section 4, item D6).
